title: POC harness acceptance criteria & streaming fallback workshop
summary: Kickoff to align on benchmark acceptance criteria, harness integration for customer scripts, and decisioning around streaming vs non-streaming traffic. Primary goals: define SLOs, workload slices, instrumentation needs, and a 2-week PoC window with clear pass/fail metrics.
topics: fallback model routing and quantization profiles
transcript:
Header: 2026-02-14 16:00 UTC | Duration: 57m
Attendees: Jesse A., Nina P., Hao C. (Redwood) — Arjun M., Maya L., Tom R., Priya R. (Vellum)
Link: POC workbook and benchmark matrix (deck) shared during call: https://redwood.example.com/poc-workbook (internal)

00:00 Jesse Alvarez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick us off. Quick round of intros then we want to get into the acceptance criteria and the harness handshake for your scripts.
00:12 Arjun Mehta: Hi, Arjun here. We're primarily focused on checkout latency and recommendation generation throughput, so this POC is make-or-break for moving to dedicated.
00:20 Nina Patel: Great, thanks Arjun. High level — we want to prove we can meet your 99th percentile latency SLOs under production-like load and show a cost/throughput profile.
01:05 Maya Lin: Quick context: we have a streaming client that sends partial user input and expects token-level updates, but for batch re-rank jobs we hit an internal batch pipeline. So we'll need both streaming and non-streaming runs.
01:42 Hao Chen: Noted. For the harness, can you share a representative client script and the live traffic histogram (inter-arrival times and token lengths)? That will let us tune batching and buffer windows.
02:10 Tom Reeves: We'll provide a sample of the live traffic plus a synthetic slow-start that simulates cold sessions. Expect a mix: 65% short prompts (~30 tokens), 25% mid (~150 tokens), 10% long (~600 tokens).
03:00 Jesse Alvarez: Good, that mix helps. Proposed acceptance criteria draft: 99th percentile latency for streaming updates under target load < 600ms for short/mid prompts; throughput sustained 80 QPS for non-streaming gen with mean tokens 150; cold-start tail (first request after idle) under 2.5s. Also model output fidelity — no measurable regression vs your golden prompts.
04:12 Priya Rao: Can you quantify "fidelity"? We need a clear pass/fail.
04:33 Nina Patel: We'll run an eval set you provide — automated rouge/EM-like metrics or embedding-similarity thresholds. If the degradation is >2% on your key prompts, we flag it as a failure. We'll include human spot checks.
05:20 Arjun Mehta: Ok. On the streaming side, we care about per-token cost and fallback behavior. If the primary model hits capacity, we need predictable fallthrough to a quantized variant with graceful quality drop.
06:02 Hao Chen: Our runtime supports automatic fallbacks by policy — you can set a latency-first policy that routes to smaller quantized variants if queued time exceeds threshold. We'll demonstrate that in the PoC. It will be part of the acceptance matrix.
07:00 Tom Reeves: How do you handle KV cache warmups for session-based re-rank tasks? Cold runs spike a lot.
07:30 Nina Patel: We recommend a KV pre-warm step in the harness — replay recent tokens to prime the cache prior to measuring steady-state. Also the harness has a warmup period that the scripts can call via an API endpoint.
08:05 Maya Lin: We already have a replay tool that can emit traffic at time offsets; we'll adapt that. For streaming, what's the recommended gRPC chunk size / flush interval? We don't want huge frame latency.
08:30 Hao Chen: Typically 100-200ms flushes for interactive UX. If you flush too often the overhead rises; too infrequent and the perceived latency worsens. Our harness can emulate different flush intervals and measure perceived latency vs token cost.
09:45 Jesse Alvarez: On instrumentation — we need request IDs propagated end-to-end, token-level latency, kernel-level GPU busy metrics, and model-variant tags. The benchmark matrix should include those telemetry columns.
10:30 Arjun Mehta: We'll require audit logs and SSO for the private deployment later. For the hosted PoC run, encrypted logs stored for 30 days is fine. Also need to see per-route cost breakdown.
11:05 Nina Patel: We'll provide a telemetry contract doc and an example tracing payload. Expect the harness to emit traces that match your request id.
12:00 Maya Lin: Any limitations around TLS termination and load balancers? Our infra terminates at the edge and load balancer does mTLS to Redwood.
12:30 Hao Chen: That's fine — we support mTLS. For Vellum's on-prem path later we can swap to a private control plane. For now just share your cert chain.
13:20 Tom Reeves: What's the expected duration of the PoC and the recommended cadence?
13:40 Jesse Alvarez: We propose a 2-week active benchmark window: week 1 - integration, warmups, single-variant baseline runs; week 2 - stress runs, fallbacks, and fidelity checks. You'll get daily brief notes and a mid-run health sync.
14:20 Priya Rao: Sounds good. What about cost estimates for the harness runs? We need a ballpark to budget engineering time.
14:40 Nina Patel: We'll share a cost matrix based on your load profile — roughly a host-hour estimate plus token cost. We'll send a spreadsheet.
15:10 Arjun Mehta: Regarding acceptance, can you include rollback criteria? If fidelity drops but latency is met, we need an action.
15:35 Hao Chen: Yes — acceptance has a hard-fail on fidelity and soft-fail on cost. We'll recommend A/B canary if results are borderline and include manual sign-off.
16:00 Maya Lin: For the harness adapter, we need a small shim library that maps our internal request format to the harness API and preserves streaming frames. How do you prefer to receive that?
16:25 Nina Patel: Zip up a sample script and send to us in the repo. We'll provide a reference adapter in Python and Node. We'll ask for a matching schema for interleaved events.
17:05 Tom Reeves: Metrics: we want p50/p95/p99 for latency, token per second, GPU utilization, cold-start distribution, and error rates. Also tail latency curves.
17:45 Jesse Alvarez: Agreed. We'll include those charts in the benchmark report.
18:10 Arjun Mehta: Any thoughts on client-side rate shaping to avoid transient queue storms?
18:30 Hao Chen: Use leaky-bucket smoothing on the client and a small jitter to reduce synchronized bursts. The harness can replay traffic with inter-arrival jitter to emulate that.
19:12 Maya Lin: For the fallback flows, how visible will the quality drop be? We need to know if there's a clear metric to trigger auto-fallback.
19:35 Nina Patel: We'll instrument delta in embedding similarity per prompt and a simple composite score. If the delta crosses your threshold and queue time exceeds X ms we flip policies. We'll demo threshold tuning.
20:50 Jesse Alvarez: Let's confirm deliverables: 1) benchmark matrix + spreadsheet; 2) reference harness adapter; 3) telemetry contract and example traces; 4) runbook for streaming vs non-streaming acceptance; 5) draft PoC schedule.
21:15 Priya Rao: Agreed. Also please include a short remediation checklist if the PoC fails — e.g., recommend model quant level, batching tweaks, or route to Dedicated.
22:05 Hao Chen: We'll include remediation suggestions with estimated impact on latency/cost.
23:00 Arjun Mehta: Endpoint security question — do you support SAML SSO for the console and audit exports?
23:20 Nina Patel: Yes, SAML and SCIM for provisioning. We'll share our security datasheet (SOC2/ISO) and default retention policies.
24:00 Maya Lin: On more technical detail — are you going to record GPU kernel latency breakdowns per token? We need to know if attention compute spikes cause the tail.
24:30 Hao Chen: Yes, the runtime collects kernel timings and can correlate with token positions. We'll include example flamegraphs.
25:10 Tom Reeves: Do you allow us to run a canary on Dedicated capacity if we decide to move forward mid-PoC?
25:30 Jesse Alvarez: We can provision a small dedicated pool but that would be a separate commercial agreement. We can simulate dedicated constraints in hosted to validate behavior.
26:00 Arjun Mehta: Ok good. Timeline and due dates?
26:20 Jesse Alvarez: Action items today: we'll send the benchmark spreadsheet and a stub adapter by 2026-02-16. You deliver sample scripts and traffic histograms by 2026-02-20. We'll schedule integration the week of Feb 23 and an active run Mar 2-13.
26:50 Priya Rao: Works for us.
27:10 Maya Lin: Small question — metrics tagging for multi-tenant logs? We need customer-scoped tags.
27:30 Hao Chen: We'll add a customer_id tag and route-level tags. The logs in the PoC will show those fields.
28:00 Jesse Alvarez: Any final Qs?
28:12 Arjun Mehta: Not from me. Looking forward to the spreadsheet and the adapter.
28:20 Jesse Alvarez: Great thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the deck and the telemetry contract.
28:28 Tom Reeves: Thanks, bye.
28:30 End of recording.
